Subject: Packaging options + fallback plan question

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. As we start to map internal usage to pricing, two things came up from our engineering and procurement teams:

1) If we want to try a lower-cost quantized model variant during peak hours, what does the fallback path look like if quality regressions appear (e.g., automatic rollback, manual switch, or mixed routing)?
2) Do you offer any one-time credits or prorated discounts if we downgrade from a higher-tier/kicked-off Dedicated reservation to a smaller seat footprint mid-term?

I attached a CSV with sample token usage and expected peaks. Can you share an example packaging matrix that includes a quantization-credit line item and a rollback playbook? Procurement will also want a sample amendment for term changes.

Best,
Sam

[Attachment: initial_usage.csv (csv, 12KB)]

Subject: Re: Packaging options + fallback plan question

Hi Sam — great to hear from you. Glad the demo was useful.

Short answers up front:
- Fallbacks: we support both automated and manual fallbacks. Policy-driven routing lets you prefer a quantized variant and fail over to the full-precision variant when a quality threshold or latency SLO is missed. We can surface that in the Console and tie it to per-route rollout rules.
- Credits: we have a structured credit approach for downgrade events. Depending on the billing model (metered vs. reserved), you may get a prorated credit toward future usage or a one-time amendment credit for the remainder of the commitment.

Attached is a packaging_matrix.xlsx with three recommended configurations (Pilot, Elastic, and Dedicated-reserved), plus a "quantization credit" row that maps approximate $/1000-token reductions for 8-bit quantized variants. Also included: quant_credit_mapping.csv which shows how credits would apply if you move between tiers mid-term.

Can you confirm: is the priority minimizing immediate spend (short-term pilot) or avoiding quality risk (long-term production)? That will change which mix we recommend.

Next steps I propose:
1) We sketch a rollback playbook (short doc) that maps triggers and the exact routing rule change.
2) Stephanie in Finance will draft the amendment language for a one-time credit if you decide to down-tier during the first 90 days.
3) If you're comfortable, we can spin up a 2-week pilot on the Elastic config and enable prefix caching to reduce token spend.

Attaching the files now.

Thanks,

Hi Sam — a couple of technical notes from product/infra that I'd like you to have before you run the pilot: 

- Quantized variants (8-bit) typically reduce per-token cost ~30-45% depending on prompt shape, but the failure modes are higher for long-context generation and structured extraction.
- Routing fallback: our policy can be time-windowed to only allow quantized variants during non-peak hours, and we support immediate rollback if the A/B eval set drops below an agreed F1 threshold.
- Cache interplay: enabling prefix/KV caching often yields larger cost reductions than quantization alone for repeat prompts.

If you can share 5–10 representative prompts or eval cases, we can simulate the quality delta and recommend the concrete thresholds for automated rollback.

— Karthik
Principal PM, Serving & Optimization | Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.com]

Thanks Lauren and Karthik — this is helpful. Couple follow-ups from procurement and engineering: 

- Procurement asks whether credits for downgrades are issued as a dollar credit applied to the remainder of the commitment or as a coupon toward hosted usage. They prefer a credit on the invoice if possible.
- Engineering will compile a short eval set (5 prompts + 3 structured extraction cases) — will drop that in the Drive link you included.

Important: if we test a quantized variant in production and it causes a user-facing regression, we need a rollback mechanism that does not require a full redeploy or manual infra intervention (the product team must be able to flip routing within 2 minutes). Is that realistic operationally?

Also, procurement would like to see a sample amendment they can pass to legal.

Hi Sam — looping in a quick note on credits and amendment language.

Policy summary:
- Metered customers: downgrade-related credits are issued as invoice adjustments for the billing period in which the downgrade is processed. No retroactive cash refunds; credits apply to future invoices.
- Reserved customers: if a customer reduces reserved capacity mid-term, we offer a prorated credit equal to the unused committed months multiplied by the reserved discount differential (example in the attached amendment draft).
- One-time pilot credit: for new customers moving from Pilot -> Elastic -> Reserved within the first 90 days, we can provide a one-time "quantization trial credit" (applied as an invoice credit) up to $15k, subject to executive approval.

For the rollback question: our Console supports rolling routing policy changes in <60s for standard routes; if you require sub-2-minute guarantees, we can enable a dedicated canary route that will flip instantly when the controller detects a threshold violation. Karthik and infra can help configure the threshold.

I've attached a short amendment draft that mirrors the language we typically pass to legal. If that looks OK, I can generate a DocuSign amendment and a tracked change copy. 

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Finance & GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Lauren / Stephanie — thanks for the clarity. DataKind is happy to proceed with the Elastic pilot:

- Pilot: 2 weeks on Elastic config with quantized variant enabled during 00:00-08:00 PST weekday windows.
- Rollback: enable the dedicated canary route with a quality threshold (we will provide eval prompts by EOD). Flip must be automatic if F1 drops >6 points on the eval set.
- Credits: please apply the one-time quantization trial credit (up to $15k) as an invoice credit if we need to down-tier within the first 90 days. Procurement will review the amendment; you can send the DocuSign to procurement@datakind.org.

If you confirm, we need the DocuSign and the routing playbook (short doc) and we'll provision the pilot by Monday.

Thanks,
Sam
